messages:
maria: FYI Acme is seeing widespread 503s for hosted inference in us-west and eu. Customers see fast 502->503 spikes. I pulled a worker log: it dies with GPU OOM then SIGSEGV. stack snippet below.

ajay: Ops alert came in too. Can you paste the exact log lines and container id? Also, did we roll any quantized runtime or kernel changes in the last 24h?

maria: container: infer-runner-7f8c9d. Logs:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] nvml: GPU 0 memory usage rising -> 99%
[2026-03-18T09:12:06Z] cuda: out of memory during allocate (size=1.2G)
[2026-03-18T09:12:07Z] runtime: fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1, fault addr 0x7f8b2c000000
[2026-03-18T09:12:07Z] infer-runner: backtrace: 0x55a3f2...
```

ajay: Hmm looks like a late-stage allocation hit. We did push a quant runtime tweak yesterday evening but only to canary. Hosted runs could have seen it in autoscale pools. Can we check image tag and commit for that container?

kevin: image tag is redwood/infer:2026-03-17-quant-bump.sha256:abcd1234. I also pulled dmesg from that host: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID=21543, ..." — typical OOM + illegal memory access.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: alert: infer-runner-7f8c9d exited 3 times in 2m. auto-eject triggered for the host.

sara: CS update: Acme SLA fire. They report timeouts triggered heavy client retries so token billing doubled for them in the window. They're asking for ETA and workaround. I'm on the call with them in 10m.

ajay: Short-term mitigation suggestions:
- enable fallback routing for Acme (route to model-redwood-small-3b or CPU pool)
- reduce max batch size and per-connection concurrency for hosted pool
- temporarily pin their traffic away from pools running the quantized runtime
Can ops do a config push for fallback routing?

kevin: Pushing fallback now: `rbctl routes set acme --fallback model-redwood-small-3b --scope customer`
kevin: Also lowering batchsize for hosted-pool-3: `rbctl pool update hosted-pool-3 --max-batch 8 --concurrency 4`

maria: Confirmed Acme traffic now routing to small-3b CPU pool, 503s dropped within ~15s. :thumbsup: CS notified.

ajay: Next: collect reproducible artifacts. Please collect: `docker logs`, `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q -x`, core dump (if coredumpctl found), and the runner heap profile. Run these commands on the host: 
```
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-9755.txt
docker logs infer-runner-7f8c9d > /tmp/infra-logs-9755.txt
sudo /usr/bin/nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY > /tmp/nvidia-mem-9755.xml
coredumpctl info infer-runner > /tmp/coredump-info-9755.txt
gdb --batch -ex 'thread apply all bt full' -ex 'quit' $(which infer-runner) core > /tmp/gdb-backtrace-9755.txt || true
```

kevin: Uploading artifacts to s3://redwood-debug/9755554321/ now. Link: https://s3.redwood.internal/9755554321 (internal)

maria: I grabbed a short heap snapshot from the runner before it ejected: memory spike shows KV cache ballooning during a long tool-call when context ~180k tokens. Looks like prefetch didn't evict properly and a big allocate attempted to reserve >1GB and failed.

ajay: That matches a regression we saw in prefix eviction heuristics after the kv-prefetch change in the quant path. Not all codepaths exercised on canary. Plan: revert quant-prefetch heuristic in hosted until we can validate.

sara: Customer ask: can we issue a credit for the retry billing? They were charged double because retries counted as new tokens. I opened a billing ticket and will escalate to finance.

kevin: For repro: run the internal load test that simulates the toolcall pattern:
```
loadtest --model redwood-large-13b-quant --qps 120 --concurrency 40 --context 180000 --duration 10m --toolcall "file:large-lookup.json"
```
kevin: We reproduced locally with that command in a dev pool and saw the same OOM followed by segfault after ~2-3 minutes.

ajay: Good repro. Next steps:
1) Hot rollback quant-prefetch change from canary to hosted images (ops).
2) Increase worker eviction sensitivity on hosted-pool-3 to avoid single-worker taking huge contexts (ops).
3) Run extended reproducer on staging with address sanitizer build and capture full coredump (eng-ml + eng-runtime).
4) Postmortem + action: add unit/integration test that simulates interleaved prefetch + large toolcall to avoid regression.

maria: Ops is rolling back image to `redwood/infer:2026-03-16-stable` on affected pools now. Rolling in waves to avoid mass churn.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: rollback job started for pool hosted-pool-3, wavesize=2 hosts.

kevin: After rollback and fallback routing 503s are back to baseline. Reproducer in staging still produces segfault when forced into quant path — will capture sanitizer logs and upload.

sara: Acme is off the call and CS confirmed they have minimal impact after fallback. They're still asking for a write-up and credit. I'll prepare a customer-facing summary once we have root cause.

ajay: Triage note: probable root cause = regression in quant-prefetch eviction heuristics leading to unbounded KV growth during long toolcalls -> late allocation failure -> cuda OOM -> illegal memory access -> segfault. Severity: P1 for hosted.

maria: Filing incident ticket and assigning to eng-runtime + eng-ml for fix. Ticket: INC-2026-9755. I'll add links to artifacts.

kevin: Uploaded sanitizer logs and gdb backtrace to the s3 link. Tagging: eng-runtime, eng-ml, infra.

sara: Recommended interim customer remedy: keep Acme traffic pinned to dedicated CPU pool until fix validated (ops). They accepted the suggestion.

ajay: Will work on a patch to weaken prefetch aggressiveness and add eviction backstop. Also will add an integration test that replays the exact long-toolcall sequence. ETA for patch: EOD + staging run.

maria: Thanks team. Keep updates here. I put a short note to on-call rotation so next shift knows mitigation state. :eyes:
